newsitem.title: USA: Nike tumbles on earnings outlook warning.
newsitem.headline: Nike tumbles on earnings outlook warning.

text.p: Shares of Nike Inc fell sharply after the sneaker maker warned Wall Street that its fourth quarter earnings would fall short of expectations.
The decline wiped out gains posted earlier this week when the stock rallied on rumors that billionaire investor Warren Buffet favored the sports marketing giant.
"If you're buying on rumors, sometimes you get hurt," said Doug Myers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane.
Nike Class B stock tumbled 8-3/4 to 54-7/8.
The company earlier Thursday said it expected to earn $0.51 to $0.56 per share in the fourth quarter ending May 31. The forecast came in below analysts' estimates of $0.69 for the quarter.
Nike said its forecast included a one-time pre-tax charge of $0.04 per share, mostly related to the shutdown of a manufacturing facility.
The warning triggered downgrades from Wall Street analysts.

Merrill Lynch analyst Brenda Gall downgraded the stock to near-term neutral from accumulate but kept the long-term rating steady at a buy. She cut fiscal 1997 estimates to $2.67-$2.72 per share from $2.90 and also lowered fiscal 1998 estimates to $3.20-$3.35 from $3.50-$3.60.
Also, Alex. Brown cut its rating to market performer from buy.

The steep decline in Nike shares marked a swift turnaround in market sentiment from earlier this week, when the stock gained 12 percent over two days on speculation about an investment by Buffet. The billionaire investor declined to comment on the rumor, while Nike described it as "purely speculative."
Nike's stock has been battered this year by concerns about slowing growth in its core U.S. footwear market.
Shares of other athletic footwear makers also fell. Reebok International Ltd was down 1-1/2 to 39-3/4, while Italian apparel and footwear company Fila Holding SpA fell one to 42-1/8.
